Maya Perez: Quick recon — weekly account health scan for Cobalt Finance. Focus this week: p95/p99 by route+model and streaming vs non-streaming. Noticed a p99 jump on /chat-stream for rwd-gptx-3b, raising potential renewal risk if it persists. Sharing quick snapshot and proposed actions.

Maya Perez: Metrics (7d rolling):
- /chat-stream  | model: rwd-gptx-3b | streaming   | p95=420ms | p99=1.8s  (wk delta: +60% p99)
- /chat-sync    | model: rwd-gptx-3b | non-stream  | p95=300ms | p99=700ms
- /generate     | model: open-llama-7b | streaming  | p95=150ms | p99=500ms
- /embed        | model: rwd-embed-2   | non-stream  | p95=45ms  | p99=120ms
Errors: /chat-stream 4xx spike 0.6% -> 1.9% (retries up).
Spend: billable tokens up 18% (retries + longer tails).
Notes: streaming p99 dominates account SLA risk; sync routes are fine.

Tessa Nguyen: Acked. I'll open a customer ticket and schedule an enablement call. Can you capture any recent traces or a short list of offending request IDs? :eyes:

Maya Perez: Added top 3 sample request IDs to the ticket: cf-req-22a, cf-req-22b, cf-req-22c. Also attaching quick hints: check KV cache hit rate and batching distribution, plus whether streaming chunk size changed on client side.

Jorge Liang: Looking now — preliminary from telemetry: KV cache hit rate for Cobalt dropped from 72% -> 38% after a client rollout two days ago. Batching histogram shows more small batches (~1-3 tokens) on streaming route which penalizes throughput.

Jorge Liang: Quick probe command if helpful: 
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://telemetry.internal/api/accounts/cobalt/kv-hits?range=7d" | jq .summary
```

Omar Singh: FYI from infra side — saw a GC activity spike on worker-7 around the same window. Log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-03T03:12:11Z] worker-7 eviction: KV-cache flush triggered, mem-pressure 78% -> 92%
[2026-03-03T03:12:12Z] worker-7 latency: tail 1.6s, batching loop reset
```
Could be correlated with cache thrash and client change.

Maya Perez: Good catch. If cache thrash is the cause we can: 1) request client to revert stream chunking to previous behavior; 2) enable prefix caching on their top routes; 3) propose a short-term Dedicated burst for peak windows.

Tessa Nguyen: For renewal risk scoring: if p99 stays >1.5s for >72 hours we mark as "at-risk" and escalate to AE. I'll start the playbook draft.

Jorge Liang: Quick config note — enabling prefix cache on /chat-stream improved similar accounts by 35% p99 in past k=3 incidents. Also consider bumping max batch size threshold to prefer slightly larger batching for streaming if latency SLO allows.

recon-bot: Automated scan summary: "Cobalt Finance — streaming route p99 increased beyond historical baseline (7d vs 30d) — anomaly score 0.84". Link: https://recon.internal/scans/cobalt/1745009999

Maya Perez: Action items: 
- Tessa: open ticket + AE notify if 72h rule triggers (T+0).
- Jorge: run KV hit-rate deep dive and propose caching config (T+6h).
- Omar: inspect worker GC patterns and suggest infra mitigation (T+12h).
- CS: schedule enablement with Cobalt to revert client chunking and discuss dedicated options (T+24h).

Tessa Nguyen: I'll book the enablement slot for Friday and attach a small checklist for client rollback steps.

Omar Singh: I'll attach worker logs and a short perf trace to the ticket. If needed we can spin a temporary burst pool for the account tomorrow.

Maya Perez: Thanks all — I'll update the renewal playbook doc with these notes and keep the thread current. cc @Jorge Liang for the follow-up. :thumbsup:
